verdict.reasoning: Patient states she "can't quite move my left arm... it's numb, and then I also feel some, like tingling in my fingertips" and later says "It's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse."

Onset after boxing: "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks" and then describes onset in that period. Persistence at rest: "if i'm just like resting if I'm sitting like, right now, I can feel like it's numb, and I, I actually feel, tingling right now."

Distribution: "I can feel it both in my, uh, um, you know a little bit in my elbow, and then in my arm, as well as in my hand" and "it's my second, third, and fourth finger" and "it's... the front side" (palmar). Shoulder pain with boxing: "sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder. Like if I try to... move like in boxing and stuff, I will even like... feel a little bit of, a little bit of pain."

Weakness and piano: "I will say, um, well I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed it's been kind of harder to get the notes." Not pain-limited: "No, no, it's not hurting, it's not hurting, it's, like, numb, I can't feel it." No object dropping: "have you been dropping things at all?... Patient: Yes. So not so much with the glass" clarifies she has difficulty with piano but does not report actually dropping objects like a glass.

"I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago" after a heavy drinking episode and "then after that, I was sick for probably good like two weeks. I was at home. I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something."
"I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore" and "So that's been a little bit painful, so I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that." implies as-needed use.
"Not really. I just take ibuprofen every once in a while, I take vitamin D."
"I like my my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but you know, they're just like huge pills so I, I, most of the time I just forget." indicates prescribed/used with poor adherence.
"But, vitamin D I take. And then, sometimes I take Melatonin to help me sleep." which corresponds to as-needed use.
"I know that my dad has I don't know if it it's hypo, I think it's hypothyroidism... he's got some autoimmune stuff going on, like that much I know."
"my mom, she's actually not in a great shape. She's got diabetes type two. She's got hypertension, um, she's got, gosh, what is it, ohh, yeah, she's got high cholesterol."
Patient is active: "in general, I'm, I'm pretty healthy. You know, I work out" and specifically "I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks."

"I was out, you know, drinking with, uh, friends... we were like out partying until, you know, late hours, and I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me." This indicates social alcohol use with one heavy episode.
"I can grasp a a glass but because I use my right hand most of the time, you know, I'm not left handed" indicates right-hand dominance.

Left UE paresthesia and weakness: "I can't quite move my left arm... it's it's numb, and then I also feel some, like tingling" and doctor summarises weakness. Subacute/progressive for ~2 weeks: "probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse." Distribution more than simple overuse is implied by persistent numbness/weakness despite rest, massage, and baths.

Transient monocular disturbance: "all of a sudden just couldn't see from the... left eye... that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, twenty, twenty minutes" and resolved. Demyelinating process suspected and urgent workup: doctor says "sometimes you know you do get things like MS, multiple sclerosis" and plans "an urgent, very urgent neurology referral... might entail... brain scan."
"I kind of hurt like my knuckles on my right hand. So that's been a little bit painful, so I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that." suggests mild right-hand knuckle pain from boxing.

Recent viral illness: "I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago" and "I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something." Fatigue: "sometimes I'll get kind of... Tired" and "I just felt really, fatigued and I couldn't even get myself to the gym."
"I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral... What that might entail is the brain scan and things like that."
"No, that's something we can't do. The treatment for it is actually some steroids... But, saying that, first we need to firm diagnosis." indicates no empiric steroids before diagnosis.

"if there's any weakness... progresses to your legs, or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E."
Patient acknowledges understanding: "Mm hmm, yes, OK. OK, got it... Sounds good! OK, thank you, doctor." after the plan and red flag advice, indicating agreement and understanding.

Transient left eye visual field loss: "I all of a sudden just couldn't see from... my left eye... that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, twenty, twenty minutes" and later confirmed "I think it was only maybe like twenty minutes or so... when I woke up it was gone." No seizures: "Ohh, no, no, no, no, nothing like that" when asked about seizures/fits. Occasional tired headaches and fatigue: "sometimes I get headaches but I think they're just tired headaches" and "I just felt really, fatigued."
